memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: This is the account of the heavens and the earth when they were created, when the Lord God made the earth and the heavens. — Gen 2:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This verse is a hinge in the story. The first chapter of Genesis showed us creation from a grand, sweeping view—the heavens, the earth, the sun and stars. Now Scripture zooms in, preparing to tell us more closely about the making of man and the garden. It is like a camera pulling back to show the whole landscape, and then moving in for a personal, close-up view.

Something quiet but wonderful happens here in the names used for God. Up to this point, He has been called simply "God"—the mighty Creator who speaks worlds into being. But now, for the first time, He is called "the Lord God." That word "Lord" is God's personal, covenant name, the name by which He would later make Himself known to His people as a God who draws near and keeps His promises.

Do you see the beauty of it? The all-powerful Maker of the heavens is not distant or cold. The same God who flung the stars into place bends down to know us personally. He is both mighty and near.

This is the very heart of the Gospel. In Jesus, the Creator stepped into His own creation to walk among us and call us His own (John 1:1–3, 14). The God of the galaxies wants to be known by you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you tend to think of God as distant, or as personally near to you?
- What difference does it make that the mighty Creator also knows your name?
- How does Jesus show us a God who draws close?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord God, You are mighty enough to make the heavens, yet gentle enough to know me personally. Thank You for drawing near to me in Jesus. Help me to walk closely with You today. Amen.
